structure.heading: Baseline Benchmarking Results for Cycle Time, First-Pass Yield, and Capacity Utilisation (Q1 2026)
text_content: **Baseline Benchmarking Results for Cycle Time, First-Pass Yield, and Capacity Utilisation (Q1 2026)**

The operational review covers Plant A (Austin), Plant B (Brno), and Plant C (Monterrey) for the period 01-01-2026 to 31-03-2026. Data sources included MES logs, quality inspection records, and production schedules. Metrics benchmarked were end-to-end cycle time, first-pass yield (FPY), and capacity utilisation across primary product lines. The dataset excludes planned outages and non-routine pilot runs to preserve baseline comparability.

End-to-end cycle time averaged 6.8 days at Plant A, 9.4 days at Plant B, and 7.6 days at Plant C. First-pass yield was 93.2% at Plant A, 89.1% at Plant B, and 91.0% at Plant C. Observations note that Plant B combines the longest cycle time with the lowest FPY, while Plant A posts the shortest lead time and highest FPY; Plant C is intermediate with product-family variability.

Capacity utilisation baselines vary by line and shift; consolidated utilisation will be published in follow-on dashboards. Prioritisation for lean interventions targets Plant B based on its 9.4-day cycle and 89.1% FPY, identifying highest near-term financial impact potential. Recommended actions include targeted root-cause analysis, containment to protect product flow and quality, and focused kaizen events to reduce cycle time and improve FPY toward the 95% aspiration.

structure.heading: Lean Opportunity Portfolio with Projected Financial Impact and Implementation Timeline (FY 2026)
text_content: **Lean Opportunity Portfolio with Projected Financial Impact and Implementation Timeline (FY 2026)**

The lean portfolio targets a 15% cycle-time reduction at Plant B (9.4 to 8.0 days) and a +3.0 percentage-point FPY improvement (89.1% to 92.1%) by 2026-12-31. These objectives are prioritized within the broader operational excellence scope and will be measrued at unit, line, and plant level using stadnardized cycle-time and first-pass-yield definitions. Targeting Plant B proivdes a focused proof point for replication elsewhere. Improvement activiites will include takt alignment, setup reduction, and defect root-cause elimination to secure sustianable gains before the end-of-year deadline.

Finance validated a projected 12-month gross benefit of $3.2M, with $1.4M attributable to throughput gain, $1.1M to scrap and rework reduction, and $0.7M to overtime reduction. Validation included sensitivity testing, conservative realization raets, and a requirement that benefits be tracked monthly against baseline P&L linse. Realization is expected during the 12 months following stabilization, and savings will be allocated to sustainment funds and continuous imporvement budgets. Finance will approve release of funds contingent on doc.ed kaizen results and verified operating data and audits.

no-go checkpoints at pilot completion and stabilization. Key deliverables per kaizen are standard work, mistake-proofing, doc.ed owners, and measurable countermeasures. Post-stabilization monitoring continues through 0226-12-31, with weekly operational metric reporting to senior management. Resource allocation will include engineers, production leads, and finance liaisons onsite.

spec.title: Operational Excellence Benchmarking Summary – Multi‑Plant Review
spec.subtitle: Ref: OPEX-22-06 | Date: 18 November 2025 | From: Director, Continuous Improvement

sections.heading: Executive Overview
sections.body: This review benchmarks baseline cycle time, first-pass yield (FPY), and capacity utilisation across Plants Orion (Ohio), Delta (Texas), and Summit (Ontario). The objective is to prioritize lean interventions with the highest 12‑month financial return validated by Finance. Data was collected from January through September 2025 using standardized definitions and verified against ERP production logs. Variability across sites indicates meaningful improvement headroom, particularly in flow balance and defect containment.

sections.heading: Cycle Time and Throughput Performance
sections.body: Average end-to-end cycle time for the flagship assembly line measured 42.6 hours at Orion, 37.9 hours at Delta, and 51.3 hours at Summit. Value stream mapping identified queue accumulation before final inspection at Summit, contributing 14.2 hours of non-value-added time. Delta demonstrated the strongest takt alignment but still experienced changeover losses averaging 11% of scheduled runtime. Standardizing SMED practices across all three sites is projected to reduce blended cycle time by 8–12%.

sections.heading: First-Pass Yield Analysis
sections.body: FPY results show Orion at 92.4%, Delta at 95.1%, and Summit at 89.7% for the review period. The primary defect categories were torque non-conformance (Orion), labeling errors (Delta), and calibration drift (Summit). Rework labor associated with these defects totaled 6,840 hours year-to-date, equating to $412,000 in direct cost. Implementing layered process audits and automated torque verification is expected to lift overall FPY to 96% within two quarters.

sections.heading: Capacity Utilisation and Constraint Assessment
sections.body: Measured capacity utilisation averaged 78% at Orion, 84% at Delta, and 69% at Summit, calculated against rated line capacity under standard staffing. Bottleneck analysis indicates that Summit’s CNC cell operates at 93% utilisation while downstream assembly remains underloaded, creating systemic imbalance. Orion’s underutilisation is primarily attributable to unplanned downtime, currently at 7.6% of available hours. Targeted preventive maintenance optimization and line rebalancing could raise blended utilisation to 85% without capital expansion.

sections.heading: 12‑Month Financial Impact Projection
sections.body: Finance validated a conservative scenario combining 10% cycle time reduction, 3.5 percentage-point FPY improvement, and 6 percentage-point utilisation uplift. The resulting benefit equates to $2.8 million in annualized EBITDA improvement, driven by $1.6 million in labor and overhead absorption gains and $1.2 million in scrap and rework reduction. Implementation costs, including training and minor automation, are estimated at $640,000, yielding a payback period of under four months. Prioritization sequence recommends initiating with Summit due to the largest performance gap and fastest recoverable value.

structure.full_text:
Operational Excellence Benchmarking Summary – Multi‑Plant Review
Ref: OPEX-22-06 | Date: 18 November 2025 | From: Director, Continuous Improvement

Section Executive Overview
This review benchmarks baseline cycle time, first-pass yield (FPY), and capacity utilisation across Plants Orion (Ohio), Delta (Texas), and Summit (Ontario). The objective is to prioritize lean interventions with the highest 12‑month financial return validated by Finance. Data was collected from January through September 2025 using standardized definitions and verified against ERP production logs. Variability across sites indicates meaningful improvement headroom, particularly in flow balance and defect containment.

Section Cycle Time and Throughput Performance
Average end-to-end cycle time for the flagship assembly line measured 42.6 hours at Orion, 37.9 hours at Delta, and 51.3 hours at Summit. Value stream mapping identified queue accumulation before final inspection at Summit, contributing 14.2 hours of non-value-added time. Delta demonstrated the strongest takt alignment but still experienced changeover losses averaging 11% of scheduled runtime. Standardizing SMED practices across all three sites is projected to reduce blended cycle time by 8–12%.

Section First-Pass Yield Analysis
FPY results show Orion at 92.4%, Delta at 95.1%, and Summit at 89.7% for the review period. The primary defect categories were torque non-conformance (Orion), labeling errors (Delta), and calibration drift (Summit). Rework labor associated with these defects totaled 6,840 hours year-to-date, equating to $412,000 in direct cost. Implementing layered process audits and automated torque verification is expected to lift overall FPY to 96% within two quarters.

Section Capacity Utilisation and Constraint Assessment
Measured capacity utilisation averaged 78% at Orion, 84% at Delta, and 69% at Summit, calculated against rated line capacity under standard staffing. Bottleneck analysis indicates that Summit’s CNC cell operates at 93% utilisation while downstream assembly remains underloaded, creating systemic imbalance. Orion’s underutilisation is primarily attributable to unplanned downtime, currently at 7.6% of available hours. Targeted preventive maintenance optimization and line rebalancing could raise blended utilisation to 85% without capital expansion.

Section 12‑Month Financial Impact Projection
Finance validated a conservative scenario combining 10% cycle time reduction, 3.5 percentage-point FPY improvement, and 6 percentage-point utilisation uplift. The resulting benefit equates to $2.8 million in annualized EBITDA improvement, driven by $1.6 million in labor and overhead absorption gains and $1.2 million in scrap and rework reduction. Implementation costs, including training and minor automation, are estimated at $640,000, yielding a payback period of under four months. Prioritization sequence recommends initiating with Summit due to the largest performance gap and fastest recoverable value.

Confidential — Operational Excellence Review | Page 1 of 2
